headline: It's prime fall-planting week: direct-sow spinach, lettuce, radishes, and kale now so they mature before the mid-October frost.

tasks.title: Direct-sow fall greens and roots
tasks.detail: Sow spinach, lettuce, arugula, radishes, and kale straight into the bed this week. There's still time to mature before your ~mid-October frost, and the cooler nights ahead make these cool-season crops sweeter and more tender.

tasks.title: Keep picking every day or two
tasks.detail: Pick tomatoes, zucchini, cucumbers, and beans frequently to keep the plants producing. Snip basil tips before they flower so the plant keeps pushing new leaves instead of setting seed.

tasks.title: Water new seedbeds daily
tasks.detail: Late-summer dry spells stall germination and stress plants. Keep the top inch of any newly sown fall bed moist every day until sprouts are up, and give established beds a deep soak once or twice a week.

tasks.title: Late blight and powdery mildew
tasks.detail: Coastal humidity favors late blight on tomatoes and powdery mildew on squash and cucumbers. Remove spotted or yellowing leaves, water at the soil line rather than overhead, and throw badly infected foliage in the trash, not the compost.

tasks.title: Top your indeterminate tomatoes
tasks.detail: Pinch out the growing tips of tall (indeterminate) tomatoes now. With roughly seven to eight weeks to frost, this steers energy into ripening the fruit already on the vine instead of new growth that won't finish in time.

tasks.title: Order seed garlic for October
tasks.detail: Order your seed garlic now for planting next month. Hardneck varieties overwinter best in NH, and the good ones sell out early in the season.
